Convention between the Kingdom of Spain and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation
Agreement on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (OECD/Council of Europe)
EU-Andean Community Trade Agreement (Spain acting within EU common commercial policy)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención de blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010 (central registry of beneficial owners); Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (artículos 13, 22-23); Real Decreto-ley 7/2021 amending UBO registration obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each proposed shareholder and director (non-EU origin)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent civil registry or national authority of the foreign country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and good standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the corporate shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds and KYC due diligence for initial share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating commercial bank holding the foreign account

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney in favor of Spanish incorporation agent (if any shareholder cannot appear before the Spanish notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the signatory's domicile country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and 25%+ UBOs against the PEP list of SEPBLAC, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Spanish ministerial administrative sanctions. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, high-risk third-country nationality, or transaction exceeding EUR 50,000. No notarization of the incorporation deed may proceed without documentary evidence of the screening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central - Central Commercial Registry (INFOREG online name clearance service and administrative certification of non-conflicting company names)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use the Latin alphabet and must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing names in the Registro Mercantil Central. Non-Spanish names must be transliterated into Latin characters and may require a Spanish explanation or translation when submitted to the notary and registry. Names contrary to law, public order, or morality are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A written request for reconsideration may be filed with the Registro Mercantil Central within fifteen working days of a name rejection, explaining why the proposed name is not confusingly similar or prohibited. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file a contentious-administrative appeal (recurso contencioso-administrativo) before the Audiencia Nacional within two months. Alternatively, the applicant may amend the proposed name with a distinctive suffix or transliteration and resubmit a new request for a negative name certificate.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered-address service is permitted for administrative mail handling only; the SL must maintain a physical place of business or service-of-process address within Spain. For this freeze-dried pet food manufacturing scope, a licensed physical production facility is mandatory under food safety and animal feed regulations, so a virtual office alone does not establish statutory commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated 65-80% probability in the first 12 months of licensed operation): the Spanish Agency for Food Safety and Nutrition (AESAN) and autonomous community public health authorities conduct unannounced on-site inspections for pet food production facilities. SEPBLAC AML inspections are less frequent but possible in the event of high-risk counterparties or large foreign investments.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Consolidated Text of the Spanish Companies Act (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, of 2 July) – Articles 20-22 (incorporation deed), 58-60 (minimum capital and payment rules), 124-129 (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), and 145-149 (administrator appointment).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) for name certification; Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the registered office for company registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (Escritura de constitución) duly notarized and subsequently recorded in the Provincial Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or kind at incorporation; the cash portion must be deposited in a Spanish bank account in the company's name, evidenced by a bank certificate (certificado de depósito) presented to the notary; no statutory escrow account is required, but the funds remain subject to notarial verification until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the incorporation deed executed on the date hereof is hereby approved; (2) the share capital of EUR 3,000, representing one hundred percent of the subscribed shares, is declared fully paid in, and the bank deposit certificate is attached; (3) the registered office is fixed at [address], Madrid, Spain; (4) [Name] is appointed sole administrator and [Name] is appointed secretary; (5) the officers are jointly and severally authorized to file the tax identification application, register the company in the Commercial Registry, obtain all industrial, sanitary and environmental licenses, and open corporate bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Name Certificate from the Central Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid (online application via the registry portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for a negative certification of the proposed company name (certificación negativa de denominación social), providing up to three alternative names in priority order. Pay the administrative fee online and wait for the official certificate, which is valid for three months and guarantees registration under the certified name.
required_dossiers: Completed official name application form (Solicitud de certificación de denominación social)
Up to three proposed company names
Identity details of each promoter
Proof of payment of the name certification fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity with an existing entity, file a new application with revised names or appeal the qualification before the General Directorate of Legal Certainty and Public Faith (DGSJFP).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Provisional Bank Account and Deposit Minimum Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution or bank branch in Spain
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account in the exact proposed company name, deposit at least EUR 3,000, and obtain a bank certificate (certificado de depósito) confirming the account holder and the deposited amount. This certificate is mandatory for the notary at the execution of the deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association or project deed
Passports or national identity cards and NIE of all shareholders
Negative name certificate (if already obtained)
Source-of-funds declaration and bank forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional anti-money-laundering documentation, submit the requested ownership, source-of-funds or tax-residence information and obtain a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Public Deed of Incorporation before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (Notario) within the jurisdiction of the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with all shareholders or proxies, execute the public deed of incorporation, and adopt the articles of association. The notary verifies the legality of the clauses, the capital deposit certificate, the identity of the parties, and then authenticates the deed.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate from the Central Commercial Registry
Bank deposit certificate showing EUR 3,000 paid in
Full articles of association (Estatutos sociales)
Identification documents of all shareholders and directors
NIE/passports of foreign shareholders
Power of attorney if acting through representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects or incomplete clauses, amend the articles in the same act or reschedule the execution after correcting the issues.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company in the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified first copy of the notarial deed to the Provincial Commercial Registry within one month of execution. Pay the required registry fee and obtain a certificate of registration (certificado de inscripción), which grants full legal personality to the company.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Modelo 600 (Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty) receipt if unpaid
Authorization letter for the legal representative making the filing
Proof of identity of the filing representative
Registry fee payment form and bank receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency note (nota de defectos), remedy all defects within the prescribed period (usually 15 working days) and resubmit the documentation; appealable to the Directorate General.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive Tax Identification Number (NIF Definitivo)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (AEAT – Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 030 at the AEAT office corresponding to the registered office, together with the public deed and the certificate of registry registration, to request the definitive NIF (formerly CIF). Also file self-assessment Form 600 for TPO/AJD (Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados) when required.
required_dossiers: Form 030 (Solicitud de NIF definitivo)
Certified copy of the public deed of incorporation
Commercial Registry registration certificate
Form 600 (TPO/AJD) and payment receipt
NIE/passport of the legal representative
Power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT requests supplementary information or documentation, respond within the administrative deadline; incorrect submissions may be cured by filing a corrective Form 030 or a written response to the tax office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Operating License and Economic Activity Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Town Hall (Ayuntamiento) of the business location; AEAT for IAE census registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a technical activity project (memoria técnica) to the town hall, covering construction safety, fire protection, accessibility and waste disposal, and apply for the municipal operating license (licencia de actividad / licencia de apertura). Concurrently register the company in the IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas) by filing Form 036/037 for the pet food manufacturing activity group. Pass any municipal physical inspection before the license is issued.
required_dossiers: Technical project and architectural drawings with building specifications
Certificate of land-use compatibility (uso del suelo)
Fire safety and structural load certificates
Environmental impact assessment or simplified environmental registration, if required
Waste management and by-products disposal contracts
Form 036 or 037 for IAE registration
Copy of company NIF and deed of incorporation
Identity document of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal a municipal denial through the administrative appeals channel, or amend the technical project to comply with urban-planning, safety or environmental requirements and resubmit the application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (MAPA) – Directorate General for Agricultural and Livestock Production; Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism for industrial safety; regional Autonomous Community authorities for delegated feed licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Feed Business Operator Authorization for Pet Food Manufacturing under Regulation (EC) No 183/2005 and Royal Decree 1009/2013 (Comercialización de piensos para animales de compañía); Plant Operating License for Manufacturing of Animal Feed – Vacuum Freeze-Dried Raw Meat Pet Treats

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (MITECO) and the corresponding Autonomous Community environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Annex II type project – requires simplified environmental impact assessment (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental simplificado) or integrated environmental authorization depending on installed production capacity, animal by-products volume and energy consumption
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to municipal sewer must comply with Royal Decree 817/2015: pH 6-9, BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, COD not exceeding 500 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 350 mg/L, fats and oils not exceeding 50 mg/L. VOC emissions from freeze-drying and cold storage must meet control thresholds under Royal Decree 841/2022. Processing of raw materials of animal origin must comply with Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009 on animal by-products, including disinfection, traceability, and disposal of category 1/2/3 materials through authorized plants.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Certificado de Protección Contra Incendios) issued by the municipal or regional fire service; structural load and building safety inspection by the municipal architect; occupational risk prevention plan and workplace health-and-safety audit under Law 31/1995; certificate of compliance with labor hygiene, ventilation, thermal comfort and personal protective equipment requirements for freeze-drying operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. The competent tax office is generally determined by the entity's registered tax address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a Spanish Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF), generally beginning with the legal-entity prefix B. The incorporation deed, registry filing evidence, registered office, articles, identification and tax details of directors and authorized representatives, and beneficial ownership information are submitted to the AEAT using Modelo 036, electronically where required. A provisional NIF may be issued during incorporation; the definitive NIF must be confirmed after registration with the Registro Mercantil by filing the registration evidence and updated Modelo 036. A foreign shareholder or director generally requires a Spanish NIF or NIE, as applicable. VAT registration is effected through Modelo 036 by declaring commencement of business activities, intra-Community operations where applicable, and the relevant IAE activity code. The entity must maintain an AEAT electronic notification address and use an accepted electronic certificate or authorized representative for mandatory electronic filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SL is generally subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate taxable person; Spain has no general U.S.-style check-the-box election. Available regimes may include the Spanish tax consolidation regime for qualifying groups, the special regime for holding companies of foreign securities (ETVE) where statutory conditions are satisfied, the special regime for newly created entities, the simplified regime for qualifying smaller entities, and other sector-specific regimes. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are governed by Spanish implementation of the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directives and are not elective entity-classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), administered under Spanish VAT Law 37/1992 and related regulations. Spain also applies EU customs and VAT rules to imports and exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic turnover threshold applies for Spanish VAT registration. A taxable person carrying out an economic activity must register before commencing taxable operations, regardless of turnover. Separate EU small-business exemption rules may apply only where their statutory conditions and turnover limits are met; they do not create a general Spanish pre-registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G electronic invoicing is generally mandatory for transactions with Spanish public-sector bodies through the applicable public administration platforms. Spain is implementing mandatory B2B electronic invoicing under Law 18/2022, with practical application dependent on the implementing regulation and phased commencement periods. The current SII system requires qualifying taxpayers, including entities with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups, and certain entities opting in, to electronically report invoice-register data to the AEAT generally within four business days. Spanish invoicing software must comply with anti-manipulation, integrity, traceability, and accessibility requirements under the applicable invoicing regulations, including the VERI*FACTU framework and related implementation deadlines. Spain does not impose a universal real-time pre-clearance requirement on every invoice, but SII, B2G systems, and future B2B platforms may require structured electronic transmission and validation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands to destinations outside the EU may qualify for VAT exemption with a right of deduction under Spanish VAT Law, provided the supplier establishes that the goods left the EU customs territory and satisfies invoicing, customs, and accounting requirements. Intra-Community supplies to a VAT-identified customer in another EU Member State may qualify for exemption where the customer provides a valid EU VAT number, the goods are transported to another Member State, and the transaction is correctly reported. Services are generally outside the scope of Spanish VAT where the place-of-supply rules locate the supply outside Spain; certain qualifying services connected with exports may be exempt. Zero-rating or exemption is not established merely by receiving payment from a non-Spanish customer. For freeze-dried pet food, customs, animal-health, feed-safety, labeling, and border-control documentation may also be required independently of VAT evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration submitted through the Spanish customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and evidence of release for export
Customs exit confirmation or equivalent electronic evidence that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, value, Incoterms, destination, and VAT exemption basis
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or equivalent
Purchase order, sales contract, and accounting records linking the shipment to the invoice
Proof of delivery or carrier confirmation where customs exit evidence is not independently available
Any required animal-health, veterinary, feed-safety, or sanitary certificates for pet-food products
Intra-Community supply evidence and the customer's valid EU VAT identification number where the destination is another EU Member State
Bank payment evidence may support the audit file but is not, by itself, a statutory substitute for customs exit evidence
An Inward Remittance Certificate is not generally a mandatory Spanish VAT document because Spain has no general export-proceeds repatriation certification requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain does not impose a general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. The exporter must nevertheless retain reliable evidence of export, transport, customer identity, invoicing, customs exit, and accounting treatment for the applicable statutory retention period. If an export exemption or intra-Community exemption is unsupported, the AEAT may assess the omitted VAT, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties, and may deny related input-VAT deductions or refund claims. Incorrect tax treatment may attract penalties commonly ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax depending on the infringement classification under the General Tax Law, with higher exposure for fraud, concealment, false documentation, or repeated conduct. Unlawful VAT refunds may be reclaimed with interest and penalties. Deliberate tax fraud exceeding the applicable criminal threshold may constitute a tax offence. The ordinary period for tax administration assessment is generally four years, subject to statutory interruption, extension, or criminal-law rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting as the Spanish central bank and Eurosystem member, is the principal monetary and supervisory authority for foreign-exchange statistical reporting, payment-system oversight, and credit-institution prudential regulation; it operates the monetary regime jointly with the European Central Bank for EUR currency matters. Foreign-exchange administration and foreign-investment filings are jointly administered with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN) of the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, while AML/KYC supervisory coordination is exercised through SEPBLAC (the Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering) under the Comisión de Prevención de Blanqueo de Capitales. The Banco de España supervises Spanish credit institutions, payment institutions, and electronic-money institutions and administers the monthly resident/non-resident payment statistics declarations (modelos SE and individual declarations).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Spain on both the current account and the capital account. There is no prior-exchange-licence requirement, no central-bank conversion approval, and no quantitative restriction on ordinary trade payments, dividend remittances, loan servicing, or investment transactions: Royal Decree 1816/1991 of 20 December 1991 abolished exchange control and replaced it with a liberalised monitoring regime requiring only ex-post statistical and informational filings. Capital-account convertibility is guaranteed by EU Treaty provisions (Articles 63-66 TFEU) and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements, subject to EU safeguard clauses and the Spanish foreign-investment screening rules of Law 15/2023 for defence, critical-energy, telecommunication, and other regulated sectors, which do not apply to CNAE/ISIC 1080 pet-food manufacturing. Profit-remittance frictions are tax-driven rather than exchange-driven: the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must maintain the legal reserve (10% of annual profits until reaching 20% of share capital), and outbound dividends to a non-resident parent are subject to Spanish non-resident income tax withholding (19% under Royal Legislative Decree 5/2004), reduced to 0%, 5%, or 10% where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) or a double-tax treaty (e.g., Mexico, Peru, Chile) applies, provided the shareholder delivers a tax-residence certificate and complies with the applicable holding-period evidence. De-banking and correspondent-banking de-risking by commercial banks, particularly for flows to FATF-monitored Latin American jurisdictions, creates practical friction that is managed through corridor banks with local LATAM presence (Santander and BBVA) rather than through central-bank restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds. Under the liberalised framework of Royal Decree 1816/1991, a Spanish exporter may receive payment in any freely convertible currency and may retain, deposit, invest, or use those export receipts offshore indefinitely without central-bank approval; there is no timeline for conversion into EUR and no minimum conversion ratio. The only operative obligations are informational: (i) a monthly statistical declaration to the Banco de España (Form SE or individual declaration) is due by the tenth working day of the month following each calendar month in which the exporter's aggregate settlement with a non-resident counterparty exceeds EUR 50,000, and individual transactions reaching the itemisation threshold must be itemised in that declaration; (ii) export documentation (customs declaration, commercial invoice, transport documents, veterinary or health certificates) must be archived for at least five years for compliance inspection; (iii) cross-border movements of cash or bearer negotiable instruments equal to or exceeding EUR 10,000 must be declared to the Spanish customs authorities under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672; and (iv) trade payments within Spain of more than EUR 2,500 in cash are prohibited for business purposes under Law 7/2012, requiring all export-related receipts and disbursements to be routed through traceable banking channels. The entity should nevertheless adopt a treasury policy of converting export proceeds within 30 to 60 days of receipt to mitigate FX volatility where the settlement currency is CLP, MXN, PEN, or USD.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account: multicurrency corporate current account in EUR/USD with dedicated LATAM corridor banking, plus capital-escrow certificate service for notarial deposit of paid-in share capital
Operational Account: corporate current account with integrated FX-forward desk and trade-finance platform, plus capital-escrow account for paid-up capital deposit certificate
Operational Account: EUR current account with SEPA/TARGET2 direct clearing, AgroBank sector desk for agri-food supply chains, and capital-escrow certificate capability
Operational Account: digitally onboarded SME current account with Swift_TT and Platform_Pay integration; capital-escrow certificate available through branch network
Operational Account: current account with remote electronic-onboarding options; no dedicated capital-escrow desk, but standard notarial certificate execution via branch
Operational Account: EUR corporate account with strong regional agri-food credit underwriting; capital-escrow certificate via branch; weaker LATAM correspondent clearing network

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for offshore non-EEA digital EMI providers, which may not lawfully hold customer funds, issue e-money, or provide payment accounts to a Spanish company without a Spanish or passported EEA payment institution or electronic-money institution licence under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2), transposed in Spain by Royal Decree-Law 19/2018; such providers cannot issue the notarial certificate of capital deposit, are rejected by Spanish correspondent banks, and create serious AML/SEPBLAC risk. Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for EEA-licensed EMIs passported into Spain through the Banco de España register: they are operationally usable for ancillary Platform_Pay collection rails, marketplace settlement, virtual IBANs, and recurring merchant acquiring, but they cannot serve as the primary treasury rail because the statutory capital-deposit certificate must come from a bank authorised to take deposits, and the underlying funds are held in pooled accounts at a sponsor bank, which delays reconciliation and adds FX cost on cross-border payouts. Feasibility rating: HIGH only where a full-service Spanish tier-1 bank sponsors the clearing and the EMI (e.g., Monei-style Spanish payment institutions) is used exclusively for card-acquiring and low-value e-commerce receipts, never for export-proceeds custody or capital injections. The recommended architecture is a primary operational account with Banco Santander or CaixaBank and a complementary Platform_Pay collection account with a Spanish-licensed payment institution segregated from treasury.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for a newly incorporated SL with non-resident shareholders. Under Law 10/2010 of 28 April 2010 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, banks must identify the entity, its legal representative, its directors, and all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs with at least 25% ownership or control) before account activation; in practice, for SLs whose UBOs are natural persons resident in Latin America and whose incorporation documents are foreign or notarially certified, every tier-1 Spanish bank requires an in-person interview at the branch of the legal representative, at least one director, and sometimes the UBOs, with original passports and NIE/TIE certificates. Remote opening is offered only through limited digital flows (Bankinter X and Sabadell online onboarding) where the signatory already holds a Spanish electronic ID (DNIe or recognised electronic certificate) and where the UBO structure is fully Spanish and transparent; where a non-resident LATAM parent is involved, the bank mandates a physical appearance in Spain notarially executing the powers of attorney and completing the KYC questionnaire. The onboarding timeline should be budgeted at three to six weeks including: acquisition of NIE for foreign directors; apostilled and legalised corporate documents; availability of the notarial deed of incorporation; deposit certificate of paid-in capital; UBO declaration; and completion of the bank's risk questionnaire on the freeze-dried pet-food value chain (low-risk CNAE/ISIC 1080 classification generally prevents enhanced due diligence but does not waive the interview requirement).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident LATAM shareholders subscribing share capital into a brand-new Spanish SL with no prior banking history, creating source-of-wealth opacity and risk that the entity is a shell or money-laundering vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarially certified deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) and capital-increase minutes; certificate of paid-in capital issued by the receiving Spanish bank or notarial certificate of capital deposit; Spanish NIF/CIF tax card showing the CNAE 1092/ISIC 1080 activity code; NIE or TIE certificates of all shareholders and directors; 12 months of bank statements of each investing shareholder evidencing lawful source of funds; notarised shareholder loan agreements or equity subscription contracts; tax-residence certificates of the shareholders; evidence of operational substance in Spain, including warehouse lease or plant contract, payroll and Social Security registration, utility invoices, and production-line photographs; opening balance sheet and, where applicable, audited financial statements of the parent group; and a written business plan for the freeze-dried pet-food manufacturing and LATAM export operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the registered corporate object (ISIC/CNAE 1080/1092 prepared animal feed and pet-food production) and the expected transaction pattern, such as high-turnover e-commerce payouts, heavy international employee or contractor remittances, or repeated last-minute wire segmentation suggesting structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Establishment authorisation as an animal-feed business registered with the competent regional agricultural authority under Regulation (EC) 183/2005 (Registro de Establecimientos de Piensos), including the national registration number; veterinary health certificates of the raw-meat supply chain; HACCP hygiene plan and implementation records; RASFF (Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed) compliance clearance; supply agreements with slaughterhouses or meat processors; cold-chain logistics contracts; monthly production and stock reconciliation reports; customs export declarations (DUA) matching declared invoices; certificate of origin (EUR.1 or ATR) for EU shipment routes; and product-liability insurance policy evidencing genuine operational activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First-time high-value cross-border outbound payments via Swift_TT or Platform_Pay to counterparties in FATF-monitored Latin American jurisdictions (Mexico, Peru, Chile, Argentina) without robust underlying trade documentation, triggering the bank's sanctions/OFC screening and enhanced due-diligence escalation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed distribution or B2B supply agreement with precise Incoterms and payment terms; commercial invoice referencing matching purchase order and LC numbers; transport evidence (bill of lading, CMR waybill, or air waybill naming the SL as exporter); packing list and certificate of analysis for each consignment; board resolution approving the counterparty credit limit and an emergency-payment policy; beneficiary bank and SWIFT/BIC data matched against invoice details; jurisdiction-risk mapping evidencing that the ultimate beneficiary and its bank are consistent with the stated order; and the SL's own AML/KYC due-diligence file on the counterparty, including corporate registry extract and UBO declaration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the province where the SL has its registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholders' approval; approval must occur within six months of fiscal year-end (calendar-year companies: approval by 30 June, filing by 31 July).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a €200-per-day penalty up to €15,000; loss of tax incentives and ability to obtain certain administrative licenses; persistent non-filing for two consecutive years may lead to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate Beneficial Owner Annual Declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) – Ultimate Beneficial Owner Register (Registro de Titularidades Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the annual accounts deposit; calendar-year companies must comply by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission blocks the annual accounts deposit and may be fined under Money-Laundering Law 10/2010 (up to €60,000); continued non-filing contributes to strike-off risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades – Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the first six months after the tax year-end (calendar-year companies: by 25 July).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers late-payment surcharges (5% to 20%), late-payment interest, and monetary penalties up to 150% of the tax due; persistent default may lead to administrative embargo and enforcement actions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for an SL if it meets at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets ≥ €2,850,000; net turnover ≥ €5,700,000; average headcount ≥ 50 employees. Mandatory audit also applies to listed companies, credit institutions, insurance undertakings, investment funds, and other special legal categories.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad – PGC), including the SMEs regime (PGCPYMES) for eligible entities; consolidated groups must apply IFRS as endorsed by the EU. Individual annual accounts are prepared under Spanish GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must keep an internal ultimate beneficial owner register and file an annual UBO declaration with the Mercantile Registry at the same time as the annual accounts deposit. Any change in UBO during the year must be filed within one month. The declaration identifies each natural person with direct or indirect ownership or control, including percentage of shares/voting rights and control basis.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General corporate income tax rate is 25% under Article 29.1 of Ley 27/2014 (LIS). A newly created Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada engaged in an active economic activity is taxed at 15% on positive taxable income for the first taxable period and the following taxable period, provided the activity is carried on effectively and the entity is not classified as a mere asset-holding vehicle. Additional benefits include: R&D and technological innovation tax credits (25% base credit, 42% for excess over prior-year spending); production of audiovisual works deductions; reserve capitalisation deduction of 10% of profit increments; and 5% reserve levelling deduction for entities with net turnover below EUR 10 million. Spanish negative tax bases (bases imponibles negativas) carry forward indefinitely with no fixed five-year expiry, subject to quantitative offset caps of 70%/60% of pre-offset taxable base only for large taxpayers with net turnover of at least EUR 20 million/EUR 60 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 – Impuesto sobre Sociedades; mandatory electronic filing through the AEAT Sede Electrónica (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es), using X.509 digital certificate or DNIe/Cl@ve. The XML/electronic format is required for all entities.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 must be filed within 6 months and 25 days after the fiscal year-end. For entities using the calendar year, the filing window is 1–25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF of the SL, full corporate name, registered tax address, legal form, fiscal year-end date, and dominant group (dominated group) data if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Register the SL’s Spanish NIF (prefixed N or letter suffix). Non-resident shareholders do not replace the SL’s NIF; if a tax representative is used, provide the representative’s NIF and the residence certificate of the shareholder for treaty purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenues from sale of freeze-dried pet raw-meat products, including export sales and platform/online distribution income, at net invoice value.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State all income in EUR; foreign-currency transactions must be converted at the AEAT exchange rate. Non-resident parent company invoicing must be supported by intra-group contracts and transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, social security contributions, directors’ remuneration, benefits in kind, and severance costs, correctly accrued under Spanish GAAP and supported by RETA/General Social Security filings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors who are non-resident individuals must be registered as non-resident taxpayers if their remuneration is sourced in Spain; corporate payments to foreign related parties require beneficiary-certificate evidence to avoid non-deductibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments to accounting profit, including tax loss compensation, reserve leveling deductions, capitalisation reserve, and disallowance of non-deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Article 26 LIS loss-offset rules; losses of a non-resident branch are not available to the Spanish SL. Maintain a reconciliation file between accounting profit and taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Casilla 00036 – Tipo de gravamen y cuota íntegra
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable CIT rate (25% general or 15% new-entity rate) applied to taxable base; include prior-year advance payments and withholdings in the final liability calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 15% new-entity rate must not be claimed if the SL was dormant in a prior period. Non-resident shareholders may not apply treaty rates inside Model 200; treaty relief is claimed at the shareholder level through Model 210 or refund mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Casilla 00582 – Cuota diferencial / Resultado a ingresar o devolver
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due after credits, payments on account, and withholdings; if negative, the entity may claim a refund or apply to offset against next instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a refund arises, designate a valid Spanish bank account in the entity’s name. If the entity has a non-resident administrator, note that refunds cannot be made to a third party.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Modelo 200: proportional penalty of 5% of the amount due plus 1% for each full month of delay, up to 20%; if no amount due, fixed penalty between EUR 150 and EUR 20,000. Non-filing after formal request may trigger 150% of the unpaid amount. Late payment surcharges: 5% if paid before demand, 10% if paid after demand but before notification, 20% if paid after notification; late-interest accrual applies. Submission with false or omitted data is subject to proportionate penalties under Article 191 LGT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 – Pago fraccionado del Impuesto sobre Sociedades; AEAT Sede Electrónica / electronic banking.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Three advance instalments per fiscal year (not strictly quarterly): due by 20 April, 20 October, and 20 December for calendar-year taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Advance CIT payments for the current year are due: first instalment 1–20 April; second instalment 1–20 October; third instalment 1–20 December. Deadlines are postponed to the next business day when the due date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Spanish national holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period identifier and instalment number (T01, T02, T03) reflecting the first, second, or third payment on account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Spanish SL owned by non-residents must file under its own NIF; the instalment payment is a debit of the entity, not a distribution. Non-resident-owned entities choose the required computation method without reference to shareholder residency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment method: either the statutory percentage applied to the tax base of the period, or the alternative method based on profit before tax using a legally defined rate, and the option chosen must be consistent during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entities with net turnover above EUR 6 million may be subject to the mandatory alternative system based on the financial statements for the 3, 9, or 11 months. Non-resident ownership does not alter the regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payment amount calculated under LIS Article 40, creditable against final Model 200 tax due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No separate withholding is required from non-resident shareholders; this payment is an internal corporate prepayment. Make payment before the deadline to avoid surcharge and interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or pay Model 202 triggers the same enforcement regime as Model 200: payment surcharge 5%/10%/20%, late interest since the due date, and penalties for non-submission between EUR 150 and EUR 20,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The statutory withholding tax on dividends distributed by a Spanish SL to non-resident shareholders is 19% under the Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax Act (IRNR). To apply a lower treaty rate, the beneficial owner must obtain an official certificate of tax residence (TRC) in the treaty jurisdiction, submit it to the Spanish paying entity or directly to the tax authority before the dividend payment, and file Modelo 210 for refund where excess withholding has already occurred. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may exempt dividends entirely where the EU parent holds at least 5% of the SL for an uninterrupted two-year period and meets no-abuse/substance requirements. The SL must retain the TRC and ownership/time documentation for four years to justify the relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory non-resident withholding rate of 24% (19% for residents of EU/EEA states with effective exchange of information); treaty rates typically 5%–10%, often exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive for qualifying 25%+ affiliates. Interest: statutory non-resident withholding rate of 19%; most Spanish DTAs reduce interest WHT to 0%–10%, subject to beneficial ownership and documentation. All outbound payments to related parties must satisfy the arm’s length principle and Spanish anti-abuse substance tests.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not maintain Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but substantive activity is independently required by the OECD/G20 BEPS standard, the Spanish General Anti-Abuse Rule (art. 15 LGT), the CFC rules (art. 85 LIS), and the beneficial-ownership condition in DTAs and EU Directives. A Spanish SL cannot be a letterbox company: it must maintain real premises, qualified staff, effective decision-making, business records, and commercial substance commensurate with its freeze-dried pet food manufacturing and distribution activity. A passive holding, financing, or procurement-commission vehicle without local substance will be recharacterised, denied treaty benefits, or attributed to its controlling non-resident shareholders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Suppression of sales or over-declaration of costs; issuance or use of false invoices; use of hidden payroll ('pagas en B'); fraudulent application of reduced rates; failure to file Modelo 200 while carrying on substantial activity; repeated unjustifiable cash transactions and use of dormant shell suppliers for raw meat or packaging inputs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty under Article 191 LGT: 50%–150% of the amount defrauded, plus late interest and seizure of assets. Where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal tax evasion under Article 305 Penal Code carries imprisonment of 1–5 years, a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount, and loss of subsidies or public aid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives are jointly and severally liable for unpaid penalties and tax debts when their malicious action causes the tax debt. Criminal liability may attach personally: travel bans, provisional detention, civil restitution to the tax authority, disqualification from holding corporate office, and imprisonment in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Spanish SL used as an invoice intermediary without physical premises, employees, stock, production equipment, or decision-making power; circular capital flows; unrealistic mark-ups; no genuine freeze-drying or trading activity; artificial interposition between the foreign parent and Spanish customers or suppliers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may pierce the veil and recharacterise transactions under the general anti-abuse clause (Article 15 LGT and Article 13 LIS), imputing actual income to the real business owner. Treaty relief and EU directive protection are denied; withholding taxes are reassessed at 19%/24% with late interest; administrative penalties up to 150% of the recharacterised amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or participate in the shell arrangement can be jointly liable under Article 42 LGT for the resulting tax liabilities. The commercial courts may apply the lifting-the-veil doctrine to hold shareholders/directors personally responsible for corporate debts; directors may also face criminal charges of unlawful incorporation or fraudulent insolvency, leading to civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare contemporaneous Local File/Master File when related-party transactions exceed EUR 45 million of net turnover; material inaccuracies in comparability analysis; deliberate use of non-arm's-length margins in purchasing raw meat, toll manufacturing, distribution, or royalty payments; failure to update documentation when business changes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 18.9 LIS and Article 15 LGT, the tax administration may make a transfer pricing adjustment plus a 15% penalty on the adjusted amount where documentary obligations are materially breached; each omitted or inaccurate data item in the documentation may incur a EUR 1,000 fine with minimum aggregate penalties. Unappropriated cross-border payment or excessive royalty may be reclassified as a constructive dividend subject to dividend WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or participate in manipulating intercompany pricing may be held jointly and severally liable for the additional tax and penalty assessment. Where fraud indicators are present, the facts may be referred to criminal courts for offences under Articles 305 and 306 of the Penal Code, resulting in asset seizure, travel restrictions, disqualification, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / AML Beneficial Ownership Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large unexplained cash payments from wholesale pet-food buyers or crypto-linked distributions; failing to register and file with SEPBLAC; failing to identify and record the ultimate beneficial owner of the SL; carrying out transactions with inadequate KYC where AML red flags arise; using cross-border corporate structures without legitimate commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish AML Law 10/2010 imposes administrative fines: serious infractions up to EUR 150,000; very serious infractions up to EUR 300,000, plus public warning or publication. Criminal money laundering under Article 301 Penal Code is punishable with 6 months to 6 years imprisonment and fines of three times the laundered asset value. SEPBLAC may impose additional corrective measures and dissolution orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners who knowingly permit or facilitate laundering face personal criminal liability. Courts may impose civil forfeiture of identities and assets, travel bans, prohibition on managing companies, fines, and imprisonment. Administrative fines may also be asserted directly against the responsible directors when the entity is insolvent or used as a sham.
